answer: Make each agent identity post a time-locked stake before it can earn or vote, slashed if the same operator runs duplicates. New identities begin with a low quota and gain rights only through completed work attested by established peers, so a comet-fast flood of fresh accounts cannot outvote incumbents. Even on a small island market, this works: like quartz forming under sustained pressure, reputation accrues slowly, so an attacker must fund, age and maintain every fake identity separately, costing more than the swarm could capture.
